key_insight: A validated 4D CTA pipeline can recover patient-specific ascending aortic strain maps with good agreement to finite-element reference deformations and stable median strain across segmentation sources.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables noninvasive, spatially resolved assessment of aortic mechanics that may support risk stratification and study of aneurysm or valvular disease progression.
method: nnU-Net segmentation, surface remeshing, deformable registration, and mesh-based strain estimation
Finite element synthetic 4D CT used as a controlled reference for validation
Laplace-Beltrami spectral reconstruction used to test strain robustness across spatial scales
evidence_signal: Median strain showed minimal bias versus FE-reference strain and narrow limits of agreement across observer and nnU-Net segmentations, while 95th-percentile strain varied more and related inversely to diameter, AHI, and age.
watch_item: High-percentile strain metrics are more sensitive to segmentation differences, so implementation should treat localized extremes with caution and validate segmentation quality carefully.
paper_title: Toward Reliable Patient-Specific Aortic Strain Mapping from 4D CTA: Validation, Spectral Structure, and Clinical Potential
